reproduced_vs_refuted.status: no verifier/refuter SPLIT exists: a single artifact (D4_uv_boundary.json) plays both roles
reproduced_vs_refuted.why: the factor = 5/(local sampling interval) model matches within 1 percent at 91.4% of points (median |dev| 0.00062); the misregistration negative control leaves the plateau at 5.000 and the FUV mean at 2.045 unchanged; the factor is composition-blind to 9.45e-03 while the underlying compositions span 152.5x in the UV. The alternative 'it is the registration shift' is directly falsified by the artifact's own index_unshifted control. Any deeper mechanism statement (which file carries the interval) is NOT settled by the data.

overreach_flags.issue: '~100x at 180 nm' is a median, not a value
overreach_flags.why: the ladder spans 85.4x-278.9x (factor 3.3) and Z=0 gives 156.8x. Passable as 'order 100x' but should be quoted as median 183x with range.

overreach_flags.issue: 'crossing moves redward with increasing metallicity' asserted with verdict=true on a non-monotone sequence
overreach_flags.why: the 35-level sequence has backward steps up to 1.65 nm and 15/35 crossings are quantised onto grid nodes. Supported: 'strong redward trend (rho=0.994, +20.7 nm/Z)'. Not supported: monotone 'moves'. Separately, the artifact's prose '6 small backward steps' is a miscount: the sequence it reports has exactly 4 strictly negative steps (620.00->618.35, 620.00->618.77, 618.7688->618.7687, 650.617->650.583); the boxcar-smoothed variant has 5, none has 6.

overreach_flags.issue: '~0.86-0.88 near 850 nm' true only as a median
overreach_flags.why: the lowest-metallicity level reaches 0.8559 and the highest 0.8856; 8/35 levels lie outside the quoted band.

overreach_flags.issue: binary mechanism verdicts with no uncertainty; 'physical_composition_effect: false' is stronger than the evidence
overreach_flags.why: 8.6% of points break the 5/interval model at the 1% level and 2 of 26 ladder rungs miss by >3%. More seriously, the last point (849.77 nm) is the artefact of an index CLIP: the one-index shift maps it back onto grid 845.0 nm, producing a duplicate endpoint and a spurious 2.3% dip that drives 'last_norm_wl_with_factor_different_from_1 = 849.77'. With the honest nearest-neighbour registration the factor at 849.77 nm is 0.99993, |factor-1|<1%, and the last non-unit wavelength is 326.41 nm. The physical conclusion (artefact, not physics) survives; this specific number does not.

overreach_flags.issue: D1's own machine-readable flag says boundary_consistent_across_T = False while the prose says the cross-temperature 'same' claim is supported
overreach_flags.why: under the literal rule 1 of 3 slices is outside the claimed 420-470 nm window; the claim only survives after switching to smoother definitions. The two statements are both in the artifact and read contradictory without the caveat.

overreach_flags.issue: the artifact never states a discrimination margin, and the one that exists is a tie
overreach_flags.why: shifting only level 1 from M=-0.9 to M=-0.95 makes the pooled statistic 0.9% WORSE - statistically indistinguishable. Do not quote this section as proving the level->M mapping is unique.

overreach_flags.issue: D3's own axis diagnostic reproduces D4's mis-hard-coding
overreach_flags.why: the entry 'last_108_rows: 108' is the SUM of offsets, not the count of rows with offset != 0 (which is 108). Harmless here, but it shows a second worker independently encoded the same one-index shift without flagging that the nearest-neighbour map is unambiguous (D3's own max_abs_nn_wavelength_mismatch_nm = 0.23 nm confirms nn is correct).

untested.item: calibration circularity of every sub-1% deviation
untested.detail: D3, D4 (and D1's MA smoother) all fit their scale on the same 330-850 nm band in which they then report sub-1% agreement. The residual there is a tautology, not independent validation. No worker fits the constant outside the band and extrapolates into it.

untested.item: the physical meaning and ownership of the 5.0 nm constant in D4
untested.detail: D4's model is 'factor = STEP_OPTICAL / local interval' with STEP_OPTICAL = 5.0 defined by construction as the optical band's own grid step, so the constant has the units of the independent variable. No worker identifies what physical or product quantity the 5.0 nm is, or tests 'factor = 5/interval' against 'factor = k/interval' with k free.

untested.item: which file carries the interval (integrated counts vs per-unit-wavelength)
untested.detail: D4 says this itself: 'this test cannot by itself say which file is per-bin and which is per-unit-wavelength'. D1/D2 implicitly assume photon counts and D3 implicitly assumes per-unit-wavelength flux, so the workers are not using one consistent observable.

untested.item: artefact-vs-physics control for D1 and D2
untested.detail: D4 ran registration negative controls. D1 and D2 have none: nobody asked whether the metallicity crossover or the F(6300)/F(5300) crossing is an artefact of the composition-index labelling or of wavelength-registration, even though D4 proved the two files disagree by one index over 108 of 175 rows.

the five response levels are NOT proportional in the optical band (median L_k/L_1 = 1.0220, 1.0503, 1.0877, 1.1146), so level 1 is not a scalar multiple of level 5 and the 'same c across levels' result depends on allowing a per-level c. No worker checked whether the five levels are five separate normalisation conventions.

only D2's C4 carries a bootstrap CI (12.73-28.54 nm/unit Z). D1's 27.5 nm robust spread, D3's 0.13% constant and 0.9% discrimination tie, and D4's 5.0024 plateau have no interval, no significance test, and no propagation of the wavelength-grid quantisation.
D1 reports per-slice crossovers and D2 per-composition crossings, but nobody fitted a joint model or tested whether the crossover shift with temperature is itself metallicity-dependent.
the 850 nm deficit is quoted at a duplicated/terminal grid node with no edge-effect statement; D4's own control shows the last 1-2 points are registration-sensitive.
